subject: Re: DPA clause - incident notification window & evidence handover
messages:
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-cloud.com>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Zoe Grant <zgrant@lawpartners.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access

David —

Thanks for the call yesterday. As part of Acme's procurement review I need to confirm the exact incident notification and evidence cooperation language we can expect in the DPA. Our security team is asking for the following changes to the standard template:

- Notification: 24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting Confidential Customer Data, with interim updates every 12 hours until containment.
- Scope: notification to include affected dataset, estimated impact (records count), and root-cause classification (misconfiguration, third-party compromise, insider).
- Evidence handover: we need the ability to receive forensic artifacts (sanitized logs, stack traces, KV cache snapshots) on a secure transfer within 5 business days for regulatory review.
- Subprocessors: manifest of current subprocessors + 30 days notice before adding any subprocessors with access to production keys.
- Cross-border transfers: confirmation that data subprocessor locations will be listed and that transfers comply with EU SCCs where applicable.

I attached a redline to our standard DPA with the above edits. Please let me know what is acceptable and where we may need compromise — timeline is tight as legal procurement is gating our pilot.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Counsel, Acme Cloud Services

Attachment: DPA_redline_v3.pdf
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary from our side:

- We aim to notify customers "without undue delay" and have historically committed to 48 hours for confirmed incidents; 24 hours is aggressive but not impossible depending on classification and whether the incident is still being validated.
- Evidence handover: we can provide redacted logs and forensic outputs, however we need to balance operational security and third-party privacy (KV caches may contain other tenants). Typical turnaround is 7 business days for sanitized artifacts; ramping to 5 business days would require an exception and a playbook for secure transfer.
- Subprocessors: we publish a current manifest and can commit to 30 days notice for subprocessors with elevated access; immediate blockers are those supporting ephemeral infra where advance notice isn't always feasible.
- Cross-border: we support SCCs for EU customers and can share subprocessors and their locations in our manifest.

I'll loop Neha (privacy) and Marissa (security ops) to propose concrete redline language and a short escalation path if tighter timelines are required for regulated workflows.

Proposed next step: Neha/Marissa propose a tradeoff (e.g., 48-hour baseline + 24-hour SLA for incidents with confirmed exfiltration, 5-day evidence handover + option for expedited transfer for high-priority regulatory requests). Would love Acme's feedback on what elements are absolute must-haves.

Thanks,
David
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 12:28:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access (internal)

Team —

Reviewing Acme's redline. High-level notes:

1) Notification window: 24-hour push is legally aggressive. Operationally, we need time to validate. Recommend: 48 hours (confirmed incidents) + interim status every 12h after notification until containment. Offer 24 hours only where we confirm unauthorized exfiltration of customer-specific keys or plaintext customer data and can validate within that window.

2) Evidence scope: We agree to provide sanitized logs and forensic outputs. KV/LLM cache snapshots are problematic because of multi-tenant content — we can provide derived artifacts (searchable indices, request IDs, request/response pairs with redactions) and a certificate of non-repudiation from our infra. For truly sensitive regulatory needs, propose a controlled remote forensic session (Zoom + read-only access) or encrypted SFTP transfer under an NDA annex. 5 business days baseline; expedite path to 48-72 hrs with SOC escalation and procurement approval.

3) Subprocessors & notice: Keep current published manifest + 30-day notice for subprocessors with access to customer data or encryption keys. For ephemeral infra (autoscaling providers), we can commit to same-day notification post-deployment and retrospective attestations.

4) SCCs & transfers: We already have EU SCC boilerplate; confirm specifics depending on Acme's region/scope.

I'll draft proposed redlines to the DPA (language alternatives + an annex that defines "forensic artifacts" and handling). Marissa, Stephanie — can you confirm typical evidence turnaround in practice and whether we can commit to a 5-business-day baseline?

Neha
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access (ops note)

Neha —

Operational realities: 5 business days is the safe baseline for sanitized artifacts if we need engineering to carve and scrub traces. We can often deliver preliminary indicators (TTPs, affected services, approximate record counts) within 24-48 hours for confirmed incidents.

For expedited transfers (48-72 hours), we need:
- A signed expedited evidence transfer addendum (DocuSign link suggested)
- An on-call SOC engineer allocation (cost/commitment consideration)
- Pre-approved scope for what we can hand over without endangering other tenants

I attached our "forensic-evidence-procedures.pdf" which outlines what we can and cannot produce and the expected timelines. If Acme needs full key-level data, that's a different discussion (we don't hold customer-managed encryption keys by default).

Marissa
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensic-evidence-procedures.pdf
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Zoe Grant <zgrant@lawpartners.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access

Marcus / Zoe —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled ops/legal together. Attached is a proposed compromise: redline with two paths in the incident notification section and an annex that defines "forensic artifacts" and the expedited transfer process. High level:

- Baseline: notification within 48 hours of confirmation; interim updates every 12 hours. Evidence handover: sanitized artifacts within 5 business days.
- Expedited path: 24-hour notification + 48-72 hour sanitized transfer if Acme signs an expedited evidence addendum (limited to specific incident classes) and covers SOC escalation costs.
- Subprocessors: we will provide manifest and 30 days notice for non-ephemeral subprocessors; we will notify within 24 hours post-deployment for autoscaling/ephemeral infra and provide retrospective attestations.
- Cross-border: we will attach SCCs for EU-scoped data requests and include subprocessors' hosting regions in the manifest.

I've also attached our redacted SOC 2 Type II report to demonstrate controls. If that addresses Acme's regulatory needs, we can proceed to DocuSign.

Link to redline & docs: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Acme-DPA-redline
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/Acme-Redwood-DPA

Please review and let me know any non-starters. If Acme needs faster commitment for the pilot, we can scope an expedited addendum and associated fees.

Thanks,
David
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_v3.pdf, SOC2_Type2_redacted.pdf
From: Zoe Grant <zgrant@lawpartners.com>
To: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA - incident notification window & evidence access

David / Team —

We reviewed the compromise with Acme's security and legal. The expedited addendum option is acceptable provided the documentation includes:

- A clear definition of "confirmed exfiltration" (sample thresholds + evidence types)
- A binding timeline for interim updates (every 12 hours)
- Confirmation that expedited forensics will be limited to Acme-scoped requests and that Redwood will attest to redaction of multi-tenant content where applicable

Assuming the annex and addendum include the above, Acme is prepared to proceed and route the redline to procurement for DocuSign. Please send the expedited addendum template and a copy of the SOC2 redaction notes for our records.

Zoe
Counsel, Law Partners (outside counsel to Acme)
